title: Answer a data-subject access request
summary: A DSAR looks like an ordinary email. It is a legal request with a statutory deadline. Under GDPR, respond without undue delay and within one month of receipt. You can extend two more months for complex or numerous requests, but only if you tell the requester within the first month (Art. 12(3), rule card eu.gdpr-dsar-response-deadline, EUR-Lex cited). The CCPA gives you 45 days, per the California AG's own page. Verify the requester's identity proportionately. Inventory everything you hold on them: product database, analytics, support desk, email tools, payment processor. Have counsel check the exemptions before anything goes out. An over-disclosure cannot be taken back, which is why sending is the irreversible step. Educational guidance, not legal advice; the controlling deadline is the statute's, verified at the primary source.

parts.title: Log the request and start the clock: one month under GDPR Art. 12(3), 45 days under CCPA — the extension needs notice inside month one
Verify the requester's identity proportionately — enough to stop impersonation, never a data grab of its own
Inventory where this person's data lives: product DB, analytics, support desk, email tools, payment processor
Assemble the export and draft the response: what you hold, purposes, recipients, retention, sources
Review the exemptions with privacy counsel where it's close: third-party data, privilege, trade secrets
Deliver securely by the deadline and record what was sent (or send the extension notice inside month one)
Fix the intake: a records-of-processing map and a standing DSAR runbook so the next one is routine

metadata.trigger: Someone exercises their data rights: a GDPR subject access request or CCPA request to know/delete lands in any inbox.
metadata.supportReason: The data inventory and the export assembly are agent work across your own systems; identity verification judgment, the exemptions review, and the decision to send are human, counsel's where it's close.

geoNotes.summary: UK GDPR's subject access request runs on the same one-month clock with the same two-month extension — the ICO's right-of-access guidance is the canonical employer-side playbook, including the identity-check and exemptions reality.

contextNeeded.query: the request itself and the date it was received (the clock runs from receipt)
